name: mybabynotes
description: Baby tracker built for one household sharing its babies' log — up to six adults (parent and caregiver roles) and up to ten children — with your data in one SQLite file on your server. Three taps from pocket to logged: the entry sheet opens pre-stamped with the current time and a prediction of what you're about to log (alternating nursing sides, last bottle amount, feed-vs-diaper rhythm). Entries write locally first and sync when there's signal, so 3am logging never waits on the network. The whole household, one log: everyone joins by invite — as a parent (full control) or a caregiver (logs, timers, and shifts) — and sees the same log live over websockets. Shift handoffs are a first-class flow — "I need to sleep, take him" becomes a request with a note, an auto-drafted plan from the baby's rhythm, and a handback summary instead of a "when did you…" conversation. Installable PWA (Add to Home Screen), Now/History views with since-cards, totals, 7-day charts, sleep and nursing timers, and optional web-push reminders — no cloud account, no FCM, no telemetry. First boot generates all secrets into /data/.env automatically; the first account registered claims the instance and invites the rest of the household. Everything (database + secrets) lives in the one /data share — back that folder up and you've backed up the app. For access beyond your LAN (and for installing the PWA + push notifications, which need HTTPS), put a reverse proxy with websocket support in front — Nginx Proxy Manager or SWAG both work; enable websockets for the /app path.

paths.name: Data
paths.description: All state: the SQLite database and the auto-generated .env with this instance's secrets. Back this folder up. NOTE: if you previously ran the docker-compose install, do NOT point this at that folder — its database sits one level down in data/, so the container would start on an empty database and leave your log behind. See docs/operations.md, 'Moving a compose install to the Unraid app'.

ports.name: WebUI Port
ports.description: Host port for the web app. The container serves everything (app, API, websockets) on this one port.

variables.name: APP_URL
variables.description: Optional: your public https origin (e.g. https://notes.example.com) when running behind a reverse proxy. Used in invite/reset emails and as the web-push VAPID subject (required for iOS push).

variables.name: REVERB_ALLOWED_ORIGINS
variables.description: Optional: comma-separated hostnames allowed to open websockets (e.g. notes.example.com). Leave empty to allow any origin.

variables.name: TRUSTED_PROXIES
variables.description: Optional: comma-separated IPs/CIDRs of your reverse proxy (e.g. 192.168.1.10) so rate limits key on real client addresses instead of the proxy's. Leave empty when not behind a proxy.
